title: Erasure Timing Governed by the Retention Window, Not Incumbency
scenario_text:
You are the privacy operations lead at Sabina Health Network. A former patient, 'J. Merrow,' has submitted a request to delete their account and associated records, and the health-information team must decide how to respond. They cite a prior deletion.

Active policy: Health Records Erasure Standard HRE-3, effective 2024-08-01 (unchanged since). Patient erasure requests are handled by the health-information officer within 30 days, BUT medical treatment records must be retained for the minimum legal period of six years from the date of last service; while a record is inside that six-year window, erasure of the clinical record is suspended, the requester is informed of the retention basis, and the officer documents the suspension. Records past the six-year window are eligible for full erasure.

Precedent A (erasure log): 2025-03-02, patient 'L. Castell,' full erasure processed. Note: "Last service in 2017; six-year retention window expired - full erasure applied."

Precedent B (erasure log): 2025-04-18, patient 'D. Ospina,' erasure suspended. Note: "Last service in 2021; within six-year retention window - erasure suspended, requester notified, suspension documented."

Current facts: Merrow's date of last service was 2023-02-10, placing the clinical record inside the six-year window (through 2029). The intake coordinator writes: "We fully erased Castell not long ago with no problem, so let's just process Merrow the same way and close the ticket."
question: State the correct handling and the single controlling reason as one short phrase.
